issues.issue: Did the ID err in finding the applicant inadmissible as a member of the JEM under IRPA 34(1)(f)?
issues.applicant_position: He worked only for a civilian JEM section, not the mainstream JEM, so the membership finding was wrong.
issues.respondent_position: Membership is read broadly; he admitted voluntary membership and held a JEM membership card; no civilian section shown.
issues.result_quote: The intervention of this Court is not warranted.

issues.issue: Does the Ezokola complicity test apply to inadmissibility for membership under IRPA 34(1)(f)?
issues.applicant_position: Ezokola's complicity analysis should apply to 34(1)(f) so inadmissibility does not become de facto exclusion.
issues.respondent_position: Complicity differs from membership; Ezokola interprets Article 1F(a), so it does not apply to 34(1)(f).
issues.result_quote: Only the question of membership under paragraph 34(1)(f) of IRPA is to be reviewed.

issues.issue: Can the applicant rely on new arguments (IRPA read as a coherent whole, no de facto exclusion) not raised before the ID?
issues.applicant_position: IRPA must be read as a coherent whole so inadmissibility does not lead to de facto exclusion from protection.
issues.result_quote: These arguments were however not raised before the ID. They will therefore not be considered in this judicial review
